items.title: Louis James Interview, 1959-05-25
items.q: I'd always go to John Robesher and buy his music

ctx.x: And you started on your mandolin and violin. Did you ever have any books that you learned to read or just learned by head?

No, I learned how to read by, well, you might as well say, by just looking and listening, see. Yes. I used to have a discussion around from Tibeto to New Orleans, so I'd always go to John Robesher and buy his music, you know. Yes. Before I, when I get back home, I already know the air of the song, you understand. Yeah. And I just learn the notes, see. Figure out the notes for it. And I know it nicely, you see. I know it nicely, see. You sort of sing the notes to yourself?
